transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-04 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marta Nguyen (Redwood Channel), Marcus Ortega (Helix Head of Platform), Leila Tan (Helix Dir AI), Samir Khan (Helix Cloud Arch), Tess O'Riley (Helix Procurement)
Shared artifacts: partner-playbook.pdf [link], helix-redwood-deal-sheet.xlsx [link], security-pack.zip [link]

Summary (auto): Quick partner GTM + technical scoping to align pilot, pricing, and security. Confirmed EMEA motion, pilot timeline, and data residency questions.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — small intro. I'm Jordan Lee, AE on the Redwood partnership team. We're here to do a quick alignment with Helix on the partner motion, scope the pilot, and call out any technical or contract risks.
00:18 Marcus: Thanks Jordan. Marcus here. Appreciate it. We wanted to, you know, make sure this is a clean handoff — Helix will be bundling inference into our managed analytics product and need to make sure SSO, data residency and pricing all line up.
00:32 Priya: Hi Marcus, Leila, Samir — Priya SE. I'll run the technical bits, perf questions, and pilot plan. Quick note: we'll probably ask for a small infra questionnaire after this to size dedicated vs hosted flows.
00:45 Leila: Hi — Leila. Main ask: low latency for certain inference flows (sub-200ms p95) and EMEA data processing. Also procurement wants clear reseller pricing.
00:58 Marta: Marta from channel — happy to coordinate the co-sell split and reseller lead in EMEA. I can drop the partner playbook after.
01:12 Samir: Quick one, do we need on-prem for any regulated customers or will VPC/private deployment cover it? Some of our customers demand no egress.
01:25 Jordan: Good point. We support Hosted, Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem). Private can be air-gapped or customer-managed VPC options; we should map which customers need that. For this pilot, what's the expected data residency?
01:38 Marcus: EMEA primarily, some EU-only contracts. Pilot can run in EU West region.
01:45 Jordan: Great. Priya, for the EU region we have dedicated pools and can configure the control plane so logs don't leave the region — we'll note that in the security pack.
02:05 Leila: On pricing — we want to understand partner overlay, partner credits for lead referrals, and list vs reseller pricing.
02:18 Marta: We typically do a 15% co-sell overlay and can run a joint win credit for net-new logos. I'll share standard wording but we can flex for strategic customers.
02:33 Tess: Procurement — any standard MSA amendments or flow for data processing addendums? Our legal will need to see sample DPAs and SOC docs.
02:46 Jordan: We have SOC2 reports and DPA templates. I'll push the security pack link. Also we have EEA data residency options documented in the partner playbook.
03:10 Priya: Shifting to pilot: we recommend two tracks — a sandbox functional test and a perf/latency benchmark. Sandbox: integration with Helix auth and samples. Perf: 10k concurrent infer requests or realistic shape you expect. We'll need sample payloads and target SLOs.
03:40 Samir: That 10k seems high — for the initial pilot 200–300 qps is more realistic but we need p95 < 200ms for single-turn text gen.
03:55 Priya: Perfect — 300 qps + p95 200ms target noted. That informs whether we run hosted or provision a small dedicated pool. Batching and KV-caching can push cost down but it depends on prompt shapes.
04:14 Marcus: What's the delta in monthly costs between hosted and a small dedicated pool? Ballpark.
04:27 Jordan: Ballpark: hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token/embedding rates; dedicated is committed monthly and becomes cheaper at sustained high qps. I'll send ballpark numbers — we'll do per-workload estimates in the spreadsheet.
04:44 Leila: Security: KMS for key management — do you support customer-managed keys?
04:55 Priya: Yes, KMS/HSM integrations are available in Private and Dedicated. Hosted can integrate via bring-your-own-key in some tiers — we'll note specifics in the pack. Our audit logs are per-tenant and we can provide token-level traces in Redwood Console.
05:18 Marcus: Any known blockers with Databricks integration? We're running parts of Helix on Databricks.
05:29 Priya: There isn't a direct one-click integration but we can stitch via API. Some customers run inference calls out of Databricks jobs to Redwood endpoints; we have examples in the docs. Keep in mind network egress and IP allowlists.
05:50 Samir: Egress — we need fixed outbound IPs for whitelisting. Can Redwood provide static egress ips from private deployment?
06:02 Jordan: For private we can, for hosted we typically provide ranges per region but not guaranteed single IP unless dedicated with NAT. We'll capture your constraint as an action item.
06:18 Tess: Legal question — will Redwood accept Helix as reseller on the agreement or do we need partner addendum?
06:29 Marta: We use a reseller addendum; most of the heavy lifting is via the channel contract. I'll attach a sample reseller addendum to the partner playbook link.
06:40 Marcus: Technical risk: we have a couple of customers with regulated workloads that want no logs outside customer environment. Can Redwood enable log redaction or customer-side logging only?
06:54 Priya: We have redaction patterns and can limit logs on Private deployments. For Hosted, we do retention controls and can work on a tighter SLA if needed. There may be engineering gating for strict no-logs scenarios.
07:12 Leila: From a GTM perspective, we want a tight 8-week pilot window — ship joint case studies quickly. Is that feasible?
07:22 Jordan: Yes, 6–10 week pilots are normal. We'll aim for 8 weeks. Priya will run the bench and we'll align weekly.
07:35 Priya: I'll request sample prompts, dataset sizes, and auth pattern. Also, are you planning any tool-calls/functions or structured output? That affects token usage and perf.
07:48 Marcus: Mostly structured outputs and short prompts but a small subset for longer generations. Expect average token lengths of 80–120.
07:59 Priya: Noted — that shapes batching and KV cache benefit.
08:10 Samir: What's the rollback if performance regresses after go-live? Do we have automatic fallback to a smaller model?
08:22 Jordan: We have routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; can set canary/A-B rollouts in the Console. We'll share runbooks for rollback.
08:36 Leila: Any competitors Helix is evaluating?
08:40 Marcus: We're also looking at Vertex AI and Databricks-managed endpoints for ease of integration.
08:48 Jordan: Understood — I can share a short competitive matrix highlighting latency/cost tradeoffs.
08:57 Marta: A commercial note — for co-sell we typically request joint pipeline entries and lead crediting in the CRM. Jordan can recap CRM steps after.
09:08 Jordan: Yep — I'll send the CRM entry steps and the joint-opportunity template.
09:18 Tess: Procurement needs sample SOW language on liability and data processing.
09:24 Jordan: We'll include SOW starter language and DPA.
09:30 Priya: Quick tech plug: if you expect lots of small requests, continuous batching helps reduce unit cost. If you have long-form, KV cache will help on repeated context. Both are config knobs.
09:52 Samir: For the pilot we'd like to validate both: throughput and cache hit rate. That means some instrumentation on our side to report hits.
10:06 Priya: Agree. We'll provide metrics and a lightweight instrumentation SDK snippet.
10:18 Marcus: OK timeline — if we get pricing and docs by Mon (Feb 8), we can kickoff pilot the following week (Feb 15). Procurement timeline looks tight but doable.
10:30 Jordan: Sounds good. We'll aim for that.
10:40 Leila: One more EMEA nuance: some customers require keys never leave EU — can KMS be region-locked?
10:51 Priya: For Private/Dedicated yes. For Hosted, we have region options and BYOK, but we'll confirm with security team on strict EU-only key residency.
11:07 Marcus: Any ask from partner/channel side? Marta?
11:12 Marta: Just please include a short one-pager for partners on margin, co-sell rules, and lead submission process. I'll put it in the playbook.
11:23 Jordan: Will do. Also quick note on metrics to include in the pilot success: 1) p95 latency <200ms, 2) cache hit rate >30% for repeated flows, 3) conversion of 2 pilot logos to paid in 3 months.
11:43 Leila: Agreed.
11:49 Priya: We'll instrument and share a weekly dashboard slot in the Console for the pilot.
12:00 Marcus: Great. Any final risks not covered?
12:06 Samir: Network egress and procurement timing are top two.
12:10 Tess: Legal will want the SOC2 right away.
12:14 Jordan: Action items recap: Jordan send pricing and CRM steps; Priya send infra questionnaire & pilot plan; Marta share partner playbook + reseller addendum; Helix to confirm VPC/egress constraints and security contact.
12:31 Marcus: Thanks everyone. We look forward to the deck and pilot kickoff.
12:35 Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up and set the pilot kickoff for week of Feb 15 once docs are in.

Auto-generated action item summary (end of call): Jordan: pricing & CRM how-to (due 2026-02-08). Priya: infra questionnaire + pilot plan (due 2026-02-10). Marta: partner playbook + reseller addendum (due 2026-02-09). Helix (Samir/Marcus): confirm VPC/egress constraints (due 2026-02-11).

Transcription notes: occasional word swaps (K-V cache transcribed as K-V cash), speaker overlaps at 05:10-05:30, some proper nouns imperfect (Databricks sometimes 'data bricks').
